name: Terrien Marginal Degeneration

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Terrien Marginal Degeneration

criteria.description: Progressive peripheral corneal thinning without inflammation
Superior or superior-temporal corneal involvement with intact epithelium
Superficial corneal vascularization at the leading edge of degeneration
Irregular astigmatism and visual distortion secondary to corneal thinning

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive peripheral corneal thinning with superior corneal involvement and absence of active inflammation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by slit-lamp examination and corneal topography.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Peripheral corneal thinning with intact epithelium
searchTerms: thin cornea edges with intact surface

pathognomonic.symptomName: Superficial corneal vascularization at the margin
searchTerms: blood vessels growing on cornea edge
uneven corneal shape causing vision distortion
cloudy cornea edges worsening over time
cornea becoming less clear at edges

common.symptomName: Mild ocular discomfort or foreign body sensation

occasional.symptomName: Corneal ectasia leading to irregular corneal shape

rare.symptomName: Secondary glaucoma due to angle involvement
searchTerms: increased eye pressure from angle issues
glaucoma due to eye drainage blockage
secondary glaucoma from eye angle problem

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing peripheral corneal thinning and vascularization
Corneal topography demonstrating irregular astigmatism and ectasia
other: Absence of inflammatory cells differentiates from inflammatory marginal keratitis

distinguishingFeatures: Inferior corneal thinning rather than superior
Presence of active inflammation and infiltrates
Usually associated with blepharitis or infection

redFlags: Severe ocular pain indicating possible secondary infection or perforation
references: Krachmer JH, Feder RS, Belin MW. Keratoconus and related noninflammatory corneal thinning disorders. Surv Ophthalmol. 1984;28(4):293-322.
American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern: Corneal Ectasia
